questions.help: Road traffic collisions     1 A public health problemMoreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision. Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative. Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.(Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: Road traffic collisions   1 A public health problem Road traffic collisions are among the leading causes of mortality, especially among young people.   (Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')Road traffic collisions   1 A public health problemStudies show that traffic collisions are the leading cause of death for men younger than 40 years and the fifth leading cause of death for men and women of all ages. As can be seen, as well as the loss of life, road collisions seriously reduce the quality of life of those injured in traffic collisions. questions.help: Road traffic collisions       2 Road traffic collisions can be avoidedWith thought and knowledge it is possible to work out where, when, how and why collisions occur and therefore how to avoid them.Certain circumstances related to the vehicle, the road and the environment but above all the driver, increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision or make the results of a collision much more serious. questions.help: Road traffic collisions             2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided   2.2 Factors involved in collisionsGenerally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.Not all risk factors are equally important. questions.help: Road traffic collisions             2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided   2.3 The key: Reducing the riskIt is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.In many collisions, the driver claims that the vehicle or road was an associated or main factor but the simple truth is that the driver could have behaved in a different way that would have avoided a collision. For example, if the driver had realised that the tyres were defective (by maintenance and inspection) they could have avoided the puncture (blow out) or if they had adopted an adequate speed and a safe distance when driving in the rain or snow, they could have avoided running into the vehicle ahead of them.Proper maintenance and responsible driving reduces the chances that a “vehicle factor” or a “road factor” will be a cause of a collision.(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: Road traffic collisions     RISK GROUPS  4 Risk groupsCertain groups of road users are more at risk because of their characteristics and are more likely to become a casualty.According to statistics, one of the main groups at risk are pedestrians, especially children and the elderly.Among the drivers most at risk, are young people, older people and the drivers of two-wheeled vehicles (bicycles, motorcycles and mopeds), because in the event of an accident they are more likely to be injured or die.(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: Road traffic collisions       RISK GROUPS  5 Pedestrians5.1 ChildrenMany children are involved in accidents with vehicles since the roadway and immediate surroundings are not conducive to their safety.Statistics show that in Spain 30% of children who died in traffic accidents were pedestrians. The main causes were shown to be ignorance of the law, foolish behaviour, carelessness and the general perceptual and cognitive limitations of children.Most children run overs take place at the end of the school day.(Página 251 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: Road traffic collisions       RISK GROUPS  5 PedestriansPedestrians are particularly vulnerable, because in the event of a collision they are more likely to suffer serious injury.Statistics indicate that the probability of being killed in a collision is greater on main roads than in built-up areas, mainly due to high speeds. However, most pedestrian deaths from car accidents occur on urban roads, which is where pedestrians are more often hit by vehicles.This high accident rate is linked mostly to the zone of uncertainty of pedestrians, making their movements less predictable than those of other road users, which means that the driver finds it harder to anticipate their behaviour and actions. (Página 251 del manual 'Learning to drive')
